subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What browser-login handoff boundary should the Control UI expose before implementation?
rationale: Automation can prove the missing surface, but it cannot safely choose the UX, authorization, redaction, plugin/core ownership, and passive-viewing versus write-control policy for authenticated browser state.

options.title: Read-only-first admin handoff panel
options.body: Expose status, tabs, URL/title, target context, and snapshots by default, with explicit operator-gated actions for open/focus/close, credential entry, and resume.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Defer the browser panel until the generic plugin Control UI entry-point contract lands, then implement the browser surface as plugin-owned UI under that security model.

options.title: Defer browser handoff UI
options.body: Keep the current CLI/browser.request workflow and leave browser login handoff out of the Control UI until remote browser management becomes a prioritized product area.

recommendation.title: Read-only-first admin handoff panel
recommendation.body: Expose status, tabs, URL/title, target context, and snapshots by default, with explicit operator-gated actions for open/focus/close, credential entry, and resume.

likelyOwner.reason: He supplied the canonical handoff criteria in the issue discussion and has the strongest combined browser/runtime/product-routing history signal.
